caveat: Talent-shortage figures come from an employer survey, not from hiring data.

expert.text: 75% of hiring processes will include certifications and testing for workplace AI proficiency by 2027.
Loss of critical thinking through GenAI will push 50% of organisations to require AI-free skills assessments by 2026.

line: AI skills are now the hardest to hire. Most gains depend on people, not tools.
scope: Skills, roles and change management for AI. Not the tools themselves.

sources.name: ManpowerGroup (via TechIntelPro)
sources.title: AI skills top global talent shortage in 2026

title: AI skills & workforce
why: AI development and AI literacy top the 2026 global talent-shortage list for the first time.
83% of German employers report hiring difficulties, the highest of 41 countries.
Engineers already spend about a quarter of their time directing AI agents.
